newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-Lend Lease 1st half seen up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-Lend Lease 1st half seen up.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd is expected to announce pre-abnormals net profit growth of about 13 percent when it reports for the half year to December 31 on Thursday.
Analysts contacted by Reuters anticipate the company will post pre-abnormal net profits of between A$155 million to A$162 million compared with A$140.1 million a year earlier.

Analysts said Lend Lease's half year earnings were difficult to forecast because its earnings from property development had the potential to vary sharply from half to half and because Lend Lease was coy about giving performance updates during the year.
BNP Equities analyst Linda Lyon was forecasting a pre-abnormal net profit of A$158 million for the half.
Lyon said Lend Lease's tax expense was likely to remain low because of the tax-paid dividends the company received from its life companies MLC and Australian Eagle.

Earnings from Lend Lease's financial services arm were boosted by the sale of Westpac Banking Corp warrants in the 1995/96 financial year, Lyon said, but some of the shortfall this year could be made up from a cost cutting exercise.

"They mentioned last year that they're aiming to cut their (financial services) expenses by 40 percent by June 1999," Lyon said. "One assumes that will have some effect in the current year, possibly more next year and in 1999 as it (cost cutting) gains momentum," she said.
Macquarie Equities analyst Tony Jackson said he was forecasting a net profit of A$156.1 million for the half.
"If the (analysts') range is A$155 million to A$162 million, then that would suggest that people are talking around A$315 million to A$325 million mark for the full year," Jackson said.

In September Lend Lease reported a 7.6 percent rise in net earnings of A$280.0 million for the year to June 30, 1996. The bulk of the earnings came from the company's financial services division whose profit rose 39 percent to A$211.4 million.
Lend Lease managing director David Higgins, without being specific, has said the company expects further profit gains in 1996/97.
Lend Lease shares closed 42 cents weaker at A$23.30 on Tuesday.
